subject: Problem with an apparent cut-off/maximum limit for modeled counts that's smaller than observed counts

messages.author: 8f1efc0241933334
messages.subject: Problem with an apparent cut-off/maximum limit for modeled counts that's smaller than observed counts
parts:
Hello unmarked users, 

I'm having an issue with what appears to be a cut-off or some kind of upper limit for modeled counts that's lower than my observed counts. Any help or thoughts would be much appreciated!

I have a pcount model for abundance of juvenile trout from replicated (5x) snorkel counts.  Abundance is modeled by covariates for pool habitat characteristics (pool area, location, depth), and detection probability covariates include pool habitat (pool area again) and survey characteristics (visibility, one of two snorkelers).  When I look at expected counts using the function fitted(model), I see that there's a maximum count value which no modeled counts exceed, but this value is much smaller than some of my observed counts.  I've included an image (below) of observed and expected counts to illustrate this value cut-off.  I should mention that I've also looked at values from predict (model, type="state"), and, although the predicted counts are larger, they exhibit this same sort of limit for a maximum count, which is lower than the modeled detection probability and observed counts would suggest. 

I've successfully run other models with different fish species and in different streams using all the same covariates.   Although I have a couple models that seem to have poor fit, none of the others have this issue of a cut-off for modeled counts.  At first I just looked at the model with the lowest AIC from a candidate model set of all covariate combinations, but it seems that all of the candidate models for this species/stream have the same issue. 

I've looked through my code and nothing seems to be any different from my other streams/species.  Any thoughts on what might be the cause of this?  

I sort of hate to just slap on a bunch of code and numbers, since I'm not sure how helpful that is, but I've included some below in case they provide any insight.  Please let me know if you'd like any other information, and apologies if I've missed anything obvious.  Thanks very much!

Hi Kristen,

I'm guessing that your model simply doesn't fit the data very well. You probably need more (or better) covariates to explain the high abundance at some of the sites. I don't think this is a problem with pcount().

Richard

On Wednesday, January 2, 2013 6:15:56 AM UTC-8, Richard Chandler wrote:
Hi Kristen,

I'm guessing that your model simply doesn't fit the data very well. You probably need more (or better) covariates to explain the high abundance at some of the sites. I don't think this is a problem with pcount().

Richard


On Wed, Dec 26, 2012 at 9:17 PM, Kristen Kirkby <kristen...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello unmarked users, 

I'm having an issue with what appears to be a cut-off or some kind of upper limit for modeled counts that's lower than my observed counts. Any help or thoughts would be much appreciated!

I have a pcount model for abundance of juvenile trout from replicated (5x) snorkel counts.  Abundance is modeled by covariates for pool habitat characteristics (pool area, location, depth), and detection probability covariates include pool habitat (pool area again) and survey characteristics (visibility, one of two snorkelers).  When I look at expected counts using the function fitted(model), I see that there's a maximum count value which no modeled counts exceed, but this value is much smaller than some of my observed counts.  I've included an image (below) of observed and expected counts to illustrate this value cut-off.  I should mention that I've also looked at values from predict (model, type="state"), and, although the predicted counts are larger, they exhibit this same sort of limit for a maximum count, which is lower than the modeled detection probability and observed counts would suggest. 

I've successfully run other models with different fish species and in different streams using all the same covariates.   Although I have a couple models that seem to have poor fit, none of the others have this issue of a cut-off for modeled counts.  At first I just looked at the model with the lowest AIC from a candidate model set of all covariate combinations, but it seems that all of the candidate models for this species/stream have the same issue. 

I've looked through my code and nothing seems to be any different from my other streams/species.  Any thoughts on what might be the cause of this?  

I sort of hate to just slap on a bunch of code and numbers, since I'm not sure how helpful that is, but I've included some below in case they provide any insight.  Please let me know if you'd like any other information, and apologies if I've missed anything obvious.  Thanks very much!
